purpose: A bounded working method for a residential solar seller who earns a commission or fee per installed system: how to choose and govern the licensed installer partners whose workmanship and install backlog the seller's name rides on, how to run the post-signature handoff and install-timeline communication that keeps a signed contract from decaying into a cancellation, how to administer cancellations and commission chargebacks as contract mechanisms rather than surprises, and how to convert only verified-happy, energized installs into the referral and review flow that is the single compounding asset a transaction-commission business owns.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

the seller does not hold the contractor, electrical, or structural licence and does not perform, engineer, inspect, or warrant the installation; a licensed installer partner builds, energizes, and warrants the system while the seller owns representation, expectation-setting, and homeowner communication

income is transactional - a commission or fee per installed system, paid against contract milestones and reversible by chargeback - so there is no contracted recurring revenue in this vertical and the only compounding asset is the reputation held by past customers and the referred pipeline it produces

every cycle time, backlog depth, chargeback trigger, payment milestone, adder amount, referral yield, and cancellation rate named here is a quantity to be read from the partner agreement, the installer's own job records, the commission statement, or the seller's own install ledger; this knowledge base supplies the mechanism and the verification route, never the value

right-to-cancel windows, door-to-door and remote-sale consumer-protection duties, referral-compensation disclosure rules, and review-solicitation rules are obligation classes whose current form differs by jurisdiction, contract type, and platform policy and must be verified with the issuing authority or platform before being relied on
exclusions: choosing between the commissioned-representative, dealer, and referral market models, designing or comparing commission structures and where commission risk sits at the economics level, lead-generation channel selection and its cost-quality trade-offs, honest homeowner qualification at the front of the funnel, and sales-cycle stage and pipeline math - all of which belong to the sibling solar market-models and lead-economics knowledge base; this knowledge base begins at the signed contract and at the partner who will build it

site and usage qualification, consumption analysis against a utility rate schedule, roof orientation, tilt and shade modelling, production estimation, offset design, proposal integrity and rate-escalator honesty, financing-structure literacy across cash, loan, lease and power-purchase-agreement classes, and permitting and interconnection process literacy - all of which belong to the sibling site-qualification, proposal-integrity and financing-literacy knowledge base; here those topics appear only as live-job status to be communicated, never as the analysis itself

stating any specific commission rate, dealer fee, per-watt spread, adder price, cycle-time figure, cancellation percentage, referral yield, cooling-off window length, or backlog depth as fact; every such quantity is treated only as a mechanism - where the number comes from, what moves it, and which document, statement, or job record establishes it for a given partner or deal

contractor, electrical, and structural licensing, engineering and code compliance, structural and roofing work, equipment and workmanship warranty obligations, permit drawings, inspection remediation, and post-install service and monitoring diagnostics, all of which belong to the licensed installer or the operations-and-maintenance provider and are never performed, diagnosed, or promised by the selling side

personalized financial, tax, legal, or insurance advice to a homeowner or to the seller, including whether a given incentive applies to a household, whether to litigate a chargeback, and how to structure the seller's own entity or taxes; those belong with the homeowner's or seller's own qualified advisors

high-pressure retention conduct of any kind - delaying, obstructing, or 'losing' a cancellation request, manufactured urgency to prevent a cancellation, misrepresenting the consequences of cancelling, or implying a homeowner cannot cancel - which is excluded as prohibited conduct rather than discouraged practice

review gating, purchased or fabricated reviews, undisclosed incentives for reviews or referrals, and conditioning any remedy on the removal of a public complaint, all of which are excluded as prohibited conduct and as platform and consumer-protection violations to be verified in the operating jurisdiction

competency_questions.question: How do I choose which installer to sell for when my name is the one the homeowner will remember in five years, and how do I check build quality with evidence instead of the installer's recruiting deck?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REPUTATION_AS_DURABLE_ASSET establishes why partner choice is a reputation decision rather than a pay decision, INSTALLER_PARTNER_CRITERIA_MODEL supplies the weighted criteria and the disqualifiers, and BUILD_QUALITY_EVIDENCE_GATHERING names the first-hand evidence routes - finished-install site visits, inspection and re-inspection history, punch-list closure records, and unscripted past-customer conversations

competency_questions.question: How deep is this installer's backlog really, and what timeline am I therefore allowed to state to a homeowner at the kitchen table?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INSTALL_BACKLOG_AND_CYCLE_TIME_READ describes reading stage-by-stage cycle times from a completed job cohort rather than an average quoted by a recruiter, and ties the range the seller may state to the observed spread of that cohort with the gating stage named

competency_questions.question: What in the dealer or referral agreement actually decides when I get paid and under what conditions the money can be taken back?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PARTNER_AGREEMENT_TERMS_LITERACY maps the payment-milestone clauses, the chargeback and offset triggers, lead-ownership, territory, termination, and post-termination treatment of in-flight deals, and states that the written terms govern over any verbal assurance

competency_questions.question: Should I sell for one installer or several, and what happens to my in-flight deals and my past customers if the installer fails, exits my market, or terminates me?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INSTALLER_CONTINUITY_RISK_DILIGENCE names the observable distress and stability signals and PARTNER_CONCENTRATION_AND_EXIT_PLANNING gives the concentration decision plus a pre-written exit path covering in-flight deals, unpaid milestones, and warranty routing for past customers

competency_questions.question: At signature, what exactly moves to the installer, what record proves what the homeowner was told, and from that moment which questions are mine to answer and which are the installer's?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HANDOFF_PACKET_AND_EXPECTATION_RECORD lists the packet contents and the dated expectation log, POST_SIGNATURE_ACCOUNTABILITY_STANCE fixes the seller as the homeowner's standing point of contact, and ROLE_BOUNDARY_WITH_LICENSED_INSTALLER draws the answer-versus-route line for technical, code, and warranty questions

competency_questions.question: What do I say to a homeowner during the silent weeks between site survey, engineering, permit, and install day, and how often do I say it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MILESTONE_COMMUNICATION_CADENCE defines milestone-keyed contact including the deliberate no-change check-in, who says what so the seller never contradicts the installer, and the logging of every commitment made

competency_questions.question: The job just slipped or the design came back changed - how do I deliver that news, and how fast?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DELAY_AND_BAD_NEWS_PROTOCOL requires the seller to carry the news first, name the gating stage and its owner, give the next verifiable checkpoint rather than a hopeful date, and open a written escalation with the installer

competency_questions.question: The site survey came back with a main-panel upgrade or a roof condition that changes the price or the scope - what must be re-disclosed, re-consented, and re-signed before anything continues?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CHANGE_ORDER_AND_ADDER_REDISCLOSURE requires written re-disclosure of the changed price, scope, and payment consequence, an explicit fresh decision by the homeowner including the option to stop, and a restatement of any cancellation right whose current form is verified for the jurisdiction

competency_questions.question: The panels are on the roof but the utility has not granted permission to operate and the homeowner just received a full utility bill - what do I owe them right now?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: POST_INSTALL_ACTIVATION_AND_FIRST_BILL_WALKTHROUGH covers the pre-framed dark period between install and activation, monitoring setup after activation, the first-bill and true-up walkthrough against the homeowner's own statements, and punch-list closure before the job is called done

competency_questions.question: Why did these signed deals cancel, which causes were mine rather than the installer's, and how do I keep score of that per partner?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CANCELLATION_CAUSE_TAXONOMY classifies each cancellation to a cause and an owner at the moment it happens, PARTNER_SCORECARD_AND_REVIEW_CADENCE aggregates those causes per partner alongside cycle time and escalation behaviour, and REFERRAL_YIELD_AND_REPUTATION_LEDGER shows whether the surviving installs are producing referred pipeline

competency_questions.question: A homeowner tells me they want to cancel - what am I allowed to do, what must I do immediately, and where does a save attempt stop being legitimate?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RIGHT_TO_CANCEL_AND_SAVE_ETHICS requires immediate written acknowledgement and routing through the contract's stated cancellation channel, permits at most one non-pressuring question about cause if the homeowner is willing, and prohibits delay, re-pitching after a clear decision, or any suggestion that cancelling is not available

competency_questions.question: My commission statement shows a deduction I did not expect - how do I reconcile it and dispute it without guessing?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CLAWBACK_ADMINISTRATION_AND_DISPUTE describes reconciling each deduction to a named contract trigger and a deal-level record, requesting the backup detail, disputing in writing inside the contractual window with the job evidence attached, and treating unexplained or recurring deductions as a partner-level signal

competency_questions.question: When is a customer actually ready to be asked for a referral or a review, and how do I ask without pressure, without hiding compensation, and without breaking platform rules?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VERIFIED_HAPPY_INSTALL_GATE defines the objective eligibility conditions before any ask, REFERRAL_REQUEST_MECHANICS gives the single-ask, opt-out-respecting request with disclosure of any compensation, and REVIEW_AND_PUBLIC_REPUTATION_PRACTICE forbids gating, incentivised-without-disclosure, or fabricated reviews and flags platform and jurisdiction verification

competency_questions.question: A public complaint, a bad review, or a consumer-protection inquiry has landed on a deal I sold - what do I do first, and what am I not allowed to do?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPLAINT_AND_ESCALATION_HANDLING requires acknowledgement, reconstruction of the job record and the dated expectation log, a remedy path routed to whoever owns the defect, honest attribution, and prohibits conditioning any remedy on withdrawal of the complaint or disclosing the customer's private details in public

glossary.definition: The utility's written authorization, granted after inspection and interconnection review, that allows a completed system to be switched on and to export; until it lands the homeowner has hardware on the roof and no production, which makes the gap between install day and PTO the most complaint-dense window in the job and a mandatory item in expectation-setting.

The queue of sold-but-unbuilt jobs an installer is carrying, expressed as the depth of work ahead of a newly submitted deal; it is read from the installer's own job records by stage rather than from a quoted average, and it is the quantity that turns a seller's stated timeline into either a kept promise or a cancellation.

A set of completed jobs from the same installer and roughly the same period whose stage dates - signature, survey, engineering, permit issue, install, inspection, activation - are read together so the seller sees the real spread and the slowest gating stage instead of a best-case anecdote.

The contractual reversal or offset of a commission already paid or accrued when a triggering event occurs, such as a cancellation before install, a funding failure, or a customer refund; the trigger list, the offset mechanics, and the dispute window are properties of the specific partner agreement and must be read from it rather than assumed.

The itemized list of unfinished or defective items identified at or after install - conduit routing, sealant, trim, debris, damaged tile, mislabelled disconnects - whose documented closure is one of the objective conditions separating a finished job from a job that merely has panels on it.

A cost item that appears after the original agreement because the site requires it - a main-panel upgrade, roof repair or reroof, structural reinforcement, trenching, or a de-rate remedy - and whose appearance changes price or scope and therefore triggers written re-disclosure and a fresh homeowner decision.

The homeowner's contractual and statutory ability to withdraw from the agreement, whose window, form, and delivery method are an obligation class that varies by jurisdiction, sale setting, and contract type; the seller's duty is to state it accurately, honour it immediately, and verify its current form with the issuing authority rather than reciting a remembered rule.

The pre-agreed sequence of named contacts and response expectations inside the installer organization - coordinator, project manager, operations lead - that a seller uses in writing when a job stalls or a defect appears, established before the first job rather than improvised during the first crisis.

A job that has objectively cleared the conditions that make advocacy honest: energized with activation granted, production visible in monitoring, punch list closed, first post-activation bill walked through, and no open complaint - the gate that must pass before any referral or review request is made.

The measured rate at which a cohort of completed installs produces introductions, appointments, and eventually installed deals over the following periods; it is computed from the seller's own install ledger and source-tagged pipeline, and it is the lagging indicator that tells a transaction-commission business whether its reputation is compounding or decaying.

nodes.definition: Treat reputation as the balance sheet of a business that has no contracted recurring revenue: every commission is a one-time transaction, so the only thing that carries value forward is the set of homeowners who would name you again and the installers who will still build for you. Operationally this means the seller keeps an install ledger of every energized job with its outcome state, treats an unresolved complaint as a liability that accrues, and treats a verified-happy install as the only asset that generates future pipeline at near-zero acquisition cost. The stance sets the decision rule used everywhere downstream: when a choice trades a homeowner's long-run experience for this month's commission, the long-run experience wins, because the alternative is a business that must buy every deal it will ever close. It also makes reputation measurable rather than sentimental - the ledger, the cause-coded cancellations, and the referred-pipeline share are the instruments, not testimonials.

included: the operating principle that referred pipeline is the only compounding asset in a per-install commission model
the install ledger as the register where reputation is recorded
the decision rule for trading present commission against future standing
excluded: lead-channel selection and paid acquisition economics, which belong to the market-models and lead-economics knowledge base
any claimed figure for what a referral is worth

pros.claim: Naming reputation as the asset converts vague professionalism into concrete post-sale obligations that can be checked
pros.example: an install with an open punch list is carried on the ledger as an unpaid liability rather than as a closed win, so it keeps generating follow-up until it clears

cons.claim: Reputation compounds on a delay far longer than a month-end, so the discipline costs money before it pays anything back
cons.example: declining to submit a marginal deal to hit a volume tier costs a commission now and returns nothing measurable until referred appointments appear seasons later

failure_modes: treating reputation as a marketing slogan while the operating decisions are all made on this month's commission
measuring only closed deals so the accumulating tail of unhappy energized customers stays invisible
assuming a good personal manner substitutes for a partner who builds well
acceptance_tests: an install ledger exists listing every signed deal with its current state, its installer, its cancellation cause if applicable, and whether it has cleared the verified-happy conditions
at least one written decision rule exists that names what the seller will not do for a commission, and it is the rule cited when a partner or a deal is declined
revisit_triggers: the share of pipeline arriving from past customers moves materially in either direction
a partner change or a market entry resets the customer base the reputation was built on

base.update_signal: a full year of the install ledger showing the referred share of installed deals, read against the cancellation causes and complaint count from the same period

nodes.definition: Fix the seller as the homeowner's standing human contact from signature through activation and beyond, even though the installer performs and owns the work. The stance is concrete: the homeowner leaves the table knowing who to call, gets that person answering during the survey-permit-install silence, and is never handed a phone tree as the answer to a question they asked a person. It is the ethical core of the post-sale phase in a vertical whose reputation damage comes largely from sellers who vanish once the contract is signed, and it is deliberately asymmetric - the seller cannot fix a roof penetration but can always own the communication, the escalation, and the honest status. The stance also binds what the seller may say: standing by the customer never means over-promising on the installer's behalf, and it never means absorbing a change quietly to keep the peace.

included: the seller's continuing contact duty after signature
the commitment to carry news the homeowner would rather hear early
the refusal to disappear behind the installer's support queue
excluded: performing, diagnosing, or warranting any physical work
front-of-funnel conduct rules for prospecting and appointments, which belong to the market-models knowledge base

pros.claim: A named human who answers during the silent weeks removes the single most common trigger for remorse-driven cancellation
pros.example: a homeowner three weeks past survey with no word calls the seller, gets the permit-queue status the same day, and stops shopping competitors

cons.claim: Standing in the middle means absorbing anger for defects the seller neither caused nor can repair, at a time when no further commission is earned
cons.example: the seller spends an afternoon on a crew's damaged tile with no mechanism to bill that time to anyone

failure_modes: going quiet after signature and reappearing only to ask for referrals
answering technical questions outside the seller's competence to seem responsive
promising remedies or dates the installer has not agreed to in writing
acceptance_tests: every signed homeowner has a named contact, a stated response expectation, and a record of the last contact date
a review of recent jobs shows no case where the homeowner's first status update came from a complaint rather than from the seller
revisit_triggers: job volume rises past what personal follow-through can carry, forcing a documented delegation model
a partner changes its customer-communication model in a way that overlaps or contradicts the seller's contact duty

base.update_signal: cancellation cause coding showing what share of lost deals cite silence or unreachability, compared before and after a contact-cadence change

nodes.definition: Draw an explicit line between what the seller owns and what the licensed installer owns, then use it as a routing rule for every homeowner question after signature. The seller owns representation, expectation-setting, status communication, escalation, and the accuracy of anything previously stated; the installer owns engineering, code compliance, structural and electrical work, permit drawings, inspection remediation, equipment and workmanship warranty, and every diagnosis of a physical symptom. The practical skill is answering with a route rather than a guess: a question about a hot conduit, a nuisance trip, or a suspected leak is converted into a written ticket with a named owner and a callback commitment, and the seller follows through until it closes rather than treating the handoff as the end of the duty. The boundary also protects the homeowner - an unlicensed opinion about a roof penetration can cost them a warranty claim - and it is the boundary that keeps the seller from making promises the installer never agreed to.

included: the answer-versus-route decision for homeowner questions
the ticket-with-owner-and-callback pattern
the classes of obligation that sit with the licence holder
excluded: any technical diagnosis, code interpretation, or warranty determination
system design, sizing, and production modelling, which belong to the proposal-integrity knowledge base

pros.claim: Routing instead of guessing keeps the seller credible and keeps the homeowner's warranty rights intact
pros.example: a homeowner reporting water near a mount gets a same-day written ticket to the installer's service queue instead of a reassurance that it is probably condensation

cons.claim: A hard boundary can read as evasive to a homeowner who wants an answer now from the person they trusted
cons.example: the homeowner hears 'that is the installer's call' and interprets it as the seller ducking after being happy to talk before signature

failure_modes: giving an off-the-cuff technical or code answer that later contradicts the installer
using the boundary as an excuse to stop following through on an open issue
letting the homeowner believe the seller performed or supervised the installation
acceptance_tests: a written responsibility split exists that assigns each class of homeowner question to seller or installer with the routing action for each
spot-checking recent tickets shows each technical question was routed with a named owner and a callback date rather than answered by the seller
revisit_triggers: a new partner assigns responsibilities differently, especially for service calls and warranty intake
a homeowner dispute reveals the boundary was described differently at the table than in the contract

base.update_signal: a partner agreement revision or a service-model change that reassigns intake, warranty, or escalation duties between installer and seller

nodes.definition: Build an explicit, weighted criteria model for choosing which installer to sell for, because in this vertical the partner decision is the largest single determinant of the seller's reputation and cancellation rate. The criteria span workmanship evidence, install backlog and cycle-time behaviour, crew sourcing - in-house crews versus rotating subcontractors - service and warranty responsiveness after energization, escalation reachability, financial and continuity stability, licensing and insurance verification by class with the issuing authority, equipment lines carried, and the commercial terms in the agreement. Weights are set before the first recruiting conversation so that a rich pay offer cannot silently outrank a build-quality failure, and hard disqualifiers are written separately from scored criteria: unverifiable licensing, a pattern of abandoned punch lists, or a refusal to give access to past customers ends the evaluation regardless of the rest. The output is a comparable candidate file per installer, not an impression formed in a recruiting meeting.

included: the criteria set and its weights
the hard disqualifier list
the requirement to verify licensing and insurance status by class with the issuing authority
excluded: assessing or certifying the installer's engineering competence, which is the licence holder's own regulated responsibility
quoting or comparing specific pay rates as figures rather than as agreement terms to read

pros.claim: Weighting before recruiting stops the highest-paying offer from silently winning a decision that is really about workmanship and schedule
pros.example: a partner offering the richest terms scores below a slower-paying one once abandoned punch lists and unreachable escalation are weighted in

cons.claim: A thorough criteria model takes weeks of diligence during which the seller has no partner to submit deals to and therefore no income
cons.example: two candidate installers require site visits and reference calls that push first submission out past the seller's cash runway

failure_modes: choosing on pay terms and personal rapport with a recruiter
scoring criteria that cannot be evidenced, so the model launders an impression as an assessment
skipping licensing and insurance verification because the installer 'obviously' holds them
acceptance_tests: each candidate installer has a completed criteria file with a source cited for every scored criterion
licensing and insurance status has been checked by class directly with the issuing authority or its public register, with the check dated
the hard disqualifier list is written and at least one candidate has been assessed against it
revisit_triggers: a partner's ownership, crew model, funding relationships, or service structure changes
the seller enters a new market where a different set of installers and different licensing classes apply

base.update_signal: outcome data from the seller's own jobs with each partner - cancellation causes, cycle-time drift, complaint count - which re-weights the criteria that actually predicted trouble

nodes.definition: Verify an installer's build quality with first-hand evidence before selling a single job, because the homeowner will attribute every crooked rail, sloppy conduit run, and unclosed punch item to the person who sat at their table. The evidence routes are unglamorous and all of them are available to a seller: stand in front of recently completed installs and look at array layout, penetration and flashing treatment, conduit routing and exterior aesthetics, labelling and disconnect placement, and site cleanup; ask the installer for its inspection outcome history including re-inspections and the reasons for them; ask how punch items are recorded and how their closure is proven; and talk to past customers the installer did not hand-pick, ideally ones found through public records or the seller's own network. Distinguish workmanship signals from taste, and distinguish a single bad job from a pattern by looking across a cohort rather than one showcase. The output is a dated evidence file that can be re-checked later rather than a recollection.

included: site observation of completed installs
inspection and re-inspection history as a quality signal
unscripted past-customer conversations and punch-list closure evidence
excluded: engineering review, code interpretation, or any inspection performed by the seller
structural or electrical assessment, which requires the relevant licence

pros.claim: Physical evidence from finished jobs is the only quality signal a recruiter cannot script
pros.example: three finished roofs in the same neighbourhood show consistent flashing treatment and clean conduit, matching what the installer claimed

cons.claim: A seller can only observe the visible surface, so hidden workmanship - attachment torque, flashing under the mount, wire management in the roof plane - stays unverified
cons.example: an array that looks immaculate from the driveway conceals penetration work that will surface as a leak two winters later

failure_modes: touring only installer-selected showcase jobs
mistaking aesthetics for build integrity or vice versa
collecting impressions rather than a dated, re-checkable evidence file
acceptance_tests: an evidence file exists per candidate installer with dated site observations across more than one job and more than one crew
at least one past-customer conversation was obtained through a route the installer did not control, with what was said recorded
revisit_triggers: the installer changes crew model, subcontracts more work, or scales headcount quickly
a punch-list or defect pattern appears in the seller's own jobs that the original evidence file did not predict

base.update_signal: defect and punch-list outcomes on the seller's own completed jobs, which either confirm or overturn the pre-partnership quality read

nodes.definition: Read the installer's real queue before stating any timeline, because the seller's most damaging promise is a date derived from a recruiter's average. The method is to obtain stage dates for a cohort of the installer's recently completed jobs in the seller's own market - signature, site survey, engineering release, permit submission and issue, install day, inspection, activation - and to look at the spread rather than the mean, since it is the slow tail that produces cancellations. Each stage is attributed to an owner: the installer controls survey, engineering, and install scheduling; the authority having jurisdiction controls permit issue and inspection; the utility controls interconnection and activation. Backlog depth is then read as work-ahead in the installer's own scheduling records plus crew capacity and seasonality, and any timeline the seller states to a homeowner is a range drawn from that cohort with the gating stage named and the parts nobody controls flagged as outside anyone's promise.

included: stage-by-stage cycle-time reading from a completed-job cohort
attribution of each stage to installer, jurisdiction, or utility
translating the observed spread into the range a seller may state
excluded: permitting and interconnection process mechanics themselves, which belong to the site-qualification and financing-literacy knowledge base
publishing any cycle-time figure as a general market fact rather than as this partner's observed record

pros.claim: A range drawn from a real cohort survives contact with reality, so the homeowner is never surprised by the ordinary case
pros.example: the seller states a window with the permit stage named as the usual constraint, and the job lands inside it without a rescue call

cons.claim: Honest ranges sound slower than a competitor's confident single date, and some homeowners choose the confident number
cons.example: a homeowner signs with a rival who names one specific install week, and the seller loses a deal by being accurate

failure_modes: quoting the best case observed and treating the tail as an exception
accepting an average with no spread and no stage attribution
carrying a partner's timeline read into a new jurisdiction where permitting behaves differently
acceptance_tests: a stage-dated cohort table exists for the partner in the seller's own market, with the slowest gating stage identified
the timeline language used with homeowners is traceable to that table and states the range plus the stages outside the installer's control
revisit_triggers: observed cycle times drift outside the range currently being stated to homeowners
the installer takes on a volume surge, loses crews, or enters a new jurisdiction with different permit behaviour

base.update_signal: a refreshed cohort of the seller's own completed jobs showing stage dates, which supersedes the partner-supplied read

nodes.definition: Assess whether the installer will still exist, still pay, and still honour warranty work through the life of the jobs the seller is about to sell, because an installer failure strands in-flight homeowners, unpaid milestones, and every past customer's workmanship warranty at once. The observable signals are behavioural rather than financial-statement based: how promptly the installer pays its representatives, dealers, and subcontractors; whether crews and coordinators are churning; whether the company has abruptly changed funding partners, equipment lines, or geographic footprint; whether it is growing faster than it is scheduling; whether service tickets on older jobs are being closed or quietly aging; and what its dispute and litigation posture looks like in public records. The seller also asks structural questions - who holds the workmanship warranty obligation, what happens to it on a transfer or a wind-down, and which funder or equipment manufacturer commitments survive independently. The output is a risk read that sets submission pace and concentration rather than a yes-or-no verdict.

included: behavioural distress and stability signals
questions about where the workmanship warranty obligation sits and what survives a transfer
translating risk into submission pace and concentration limits
excluded: auditing the installer's finances or forming a credit opinion
advising a homeowner on the creditworthiness of any counterparty, which is personalized financial advice

pros.claim: Payment and service-ticket behaviour surface distress earlier than any formal announcement, giving the seller time to slow submissions
pros.example: commission statements start arriving late and older service tickets stop closing, and the seller stops adding new jobs to that queue before the backlog grows

cons.claim: The signals are ambiguous and can be misread, and acting on a false read costs the seller a functioning partner and a market position
cons.example: a temporary coordinator turnover during a software migration looks like distress and prompts an unnecessary exit

failure_modes: ignoring late payments to oneself as a personal dispute rather than a systemic signal
concentrating all pipeline with a partner while its distress signals accumulate
assuming past customers' warranties are safe without asking who actually holds the obligation
acceptance_tests: a dated continuity read exists per partner listing the observed payment, staffing, service-closure, and public-record signals
the seller can state, from the agreement and from the installer's answer, where the workmanship warranty obligation sits and what happens to it on a wind-down or transfer
revisit_triggers: a payment to the seller is late or short without an explanation traceable to a contract term
ownership, funding, equipment supply, or senior operations leadership changes at the partner

base.update_signal: a change in the partner's payment timeliness, service-ticket closure behaviour, staffing stability, or public dispute record

nodes.definition: Read the dealer, representative, or referral agreement as the mechanism that decides when money arrives and when it leaves, and map its clauses before signing rather than after the first deduction. The clauses that matter operationally are the payment milestones and what documentary event triggers each, the chargeback and offset triggers with their lookback and the order in which offsets are applied, lead ownership and what happens to a homeowner the seller introduced, territory and exclusivity, submission and approval rights, the escalation and service commitments the installer accepts, termination rights on both sides, and - most often overlooked - the treatment of in-flight deals and unpaid milestones after termination. Referral-model agreements add compensation-disclosure obligations whose current form must be verified for the jurisdiction and, where the homeowner is being introduced, disclosed to that homeowner. The rule the seller carries out of this work is simple: the written term governs, and a recruiter's verbal assurance that 'we never charge that back' is not a term.

included: clause-by-clause mapping of payment, chargeback, territory, termination, and in-flight treatment
the obligation class attaching to referral compensation and its disclosure, to be verified per jurisdiction
the primacy of the written term over verbal assurance
excluded: legal advice on enforceability, negotiation strategy, or whether to sign, which requires the seller's own counsel
commission-structure design and income planning across models, which belong to the market-models and lead-economics knowledge base

pros.claim: A clause map turns a later deduction from a shock into a predictable, checkable event
pros.example: when a statement shows an offset, the seller matches it to the named trigger clause and the deal record in minutes instead of arguing from memory

cons.claim: Mapping the terms does not give the seller power to change them, and the realistic choice is often to accept or walk
cons.example: the chargeback lookback is longer than the seller would like and the partner will not amend it for a single new representative

failure_modes: relying on a recruiter's summary instead of the executed document
missing the post-termination treatment of in-flight deals until termination happens
treating referral compensation as a private arrangement when a disclosure obligation class applies
acceptance_tests: a written clause map exists naming, for each payment milestone, the documentary event that triggers it and, for each chargeback trigger, its condition and lookback
the post-termination treatment of in-flight deals and unpaid milestones is quoted from the agreement rather than paraphrased
any referral compensation arrangement has been checked against the applicable disclosure obligation class for the jurisdiction, with the verification dated
revisit_triggers: the partner issues an amended agreement, addendum, or new compensation schedule
a deduction or payment appears that the clause map does not explain

base.update_signal: an amended agreement or compensation schedule, or a statement event that the current clause map fails to explain

nodes.definition: Decide deliberately how much of the pipeline any single installer carries, and write the exit path before it is needed. Concentration buys depth - better scheduling attention, tier standing, a coordinator who knows the seller's name - while spreading buys resilience and lets deals be routed to the partner that fits the job, at the cost of thinner standing everywhere, more agreements to track, exclusivity conflicts, and a homeowner-facing story that must stay coherent. The exit plan is the harder half: it names what happens to deals in flight at each stage, which unpaid milestones survive termination and under which clause, how past customers are told where their warranty and service now live, and what the seller may and may not say publicly about a former partner. A seller who has not written this before signing will improvise it during the worst week of the business, in front of homeowners who are already anxious.

included: the concentration decision and its trade-offs
routing logic when more than one partner is carried
a written exit path covering in-flight deals, unpaid milestones, past-customer warranty routing, and public conduct
excluded: negotiating or interpreting termination rights as legal advice
any claim about how many partners a seller should carry expressed as a figure rather than as a reasoned trade-off

pros.claim: A pre-written exit path keeps homeowners informed and factual on the day a partner fails, when improvisation is most damaging
pros.example: when a partner stops scheduling, the seller sends the pre-planned factual notice and the documented transfer question the same week rather than going silent

cons.claim: Carrying a second partner dilutes standing with the first and can breach exclusivity or trigger territory clauses
cons.example: adding a second installer drops the seller below a volume threshold that had been buying priority scheduling, slowing every job

failure_modes: concentrating everything with one partner because the relationship is comfortable
adding partners without checking exclusivity, lead-ownership, and non-solicitation clauses
leaving past customers with no answer about where their warranty and service now live
acceptance_tests: a written concentration position exists with the routing rule for which deal goes to which partner and the exclusivity constraints checked against each agreement
an exit path document exists naming the treatment of in-flight deals by stage, the survival of unpaid milestones by clause, and the message past customers will receive
revisit_triggers: a partner's continuity read deteriorates or its scheduling behaviour changes materially
a new agreement introduces exclusivity, territory, or non-solicitation terms that change the routing rule

base.update_signal: an actual partner transition, or a change in exclusivity or scheduling-priority terms that alters the cost of carrying more than one partner

nodes.definition: Score each installer continuously on the seller's own completed and in-flight jobs rather than on the impression formed during recruiting, and review it on a fixed cadence with the partner. The measures are all derivable from the seller's records: stage cycle times and their drift, share of jobs with a post-install punch list and how long closure takes, escalation response behaviour against the agreed ladder, cancellations attributable to the installer's delay or conduct as coded in the cancellation taxonomy, complaint and public-review incidence traced back to jobs, statement accuracy and payment timeliness, and how often the seller had to deliver news the installer should have delivered. The cadence has two halves - an internal read and a conversation with the partner where the same evidence is shown - and it carries stated consequences: a documented improvement request, a submission slowdown, or the exit path. Scoring without a consequence is a diary, not a control.

included: the measure set drawn from the seller's own job records
the internal and joint review cadence
the consequence ladder from improvement request to submission slowdown to exit
excluded: auditing the installer's internal operations or crews
publishing partner scores externally or using them in homeowner-facing comparison claims

pros.claim: Evidence from the seller's own jobs converts a partner conversation from complaint into a reviewable record
pros.example: the seller shows a stage-dated list of jobs stuck at engineering release, and scheduling attention improves without a relationship rupture

cons.claim: A small seller's job count is a thin sample, so a scorecard can over-read noise and strain a partnership that is actually fine
cons.example: two unusual jobs in a quarter make cycle times look like a trend when they were a permit-office backlog nobody controlled

failure_modes: measuring only what the installer reports rather than what the seller observed
running the cadence with no stated consequence, so nothing changes
attributing every delay to the installer without separating jurisdiction and utility stages
acceptance_tests: a per-partner scorecard exists with each measure sourced from the seller's own job records and refreshed on the stated cadence
each review has a written outcome naming the requested change and the consequence if it does not appear
revisit_triggers: a measure crosses the threshold the seller set for a submission slowdown
cancellation cause coding shifts toward installer-owned causes

base.update_signal: each completed review cycle, which adds a period of job outcomes and either confirms or overturns the previous read of the partner

nodes.definition: Assemble, at signature, the packet that moves the deal to the installer and the record that preserves what the homeowner was actually told. The packet carries the executed agreement and disclosures, site access and scheduling constraints, utility account and roof-access details, known site conditions and homeowner-flagged concerns, and any commitment made at the table; the expectation record is the seller's own dated log of the timeline range stated with the gating stage named, the production and savings framing that came from the modelling rather than from enthusiasm, the financing structure as explained, the sequence of stages the homeowner should expect including the dark period before activation, and who the homeowner should call. The two artifacts serve different masters - the packet keeps the installer from re-discovering the job, the record protects both the homeowner and the seller when memory diverges months later - and both are created before the first coordinator call, not reconstructed after a complaint.

included: packet contents that transfer the job cleanly
the dated expectation log of what was stated to the homeowner
the stage-sequence explanation including the pre-activation dark period
excluded: the production modelling and financing explanation themselves, which are produced in the proposal-integrity and financing-literacy knowledge base and only recorded here
storing homeowner credit or financial data beyond what the process requires and permits

pros.claim: A dated expectation record makes later disputes resolvable by evidence instead of by who sounds more certain
pros.example: a homeowner recalls being promised an install month; the log shows the range and the permit caveat stated, and the conversation becomes about the current status

cons.claim: Writing everything down at signature slows the close and can feel bureaucratic to a homeowner who wants the visit to end
cons.example: the seller spends extra time at the table restating the stage sequence while the homeowner is ready to sign and go to dinner

failure_modes: handing off a thin packet so the coordinator re-interviews the homeowner and the process feels chaotic
logging only what was signed and not what was said
letting the expectation record drift from the disclosures actually given
acceptance_tests: every signed deal has a handoff packet with the listed contents and a dated expectation log created before the first installer contact
the expectation log's timeline language matches the cohort-derived range, with the gating stage named
revisit_triggers: the partner changes its intake requirements or its customer-facing stage language
a dispute reveals a gap between what the log recorded and what the homeowner understood

base.update_signal: disputes or cancellations whose cause coding points at an expectation the log did not capture, prompting a revision of what the record must contain

nodes.definition: Run a contact cadence keyed to job milestones so the homeowner never has to wonder whether they have been forgotten between signature and activation. Each stage transition - survey scheduled, survey complete, engineering released, permit submitted, permit issued, install scheduled, install complete, inspection passed, activation granted - produces a short factual update naming what just happened, what is next, who owns it, and when the next update will come; on top of that sits the deliberate no-change check-in, which exists precisely because nothing happened and silence is what breeds remorse. The seller states only what the installer's records support, never a date the installer has not committed in writing, and logs every contact and every commitment made so the record stays consistent with the expectation log. The cadence is also the cheapest cancellation control the business has: most of the deals lost after signature are lost during the quiet, not during the crisis.

included: milestone-triggered updates and the no-change check-in
the rule that only installer-supported status is stated
logging of contacts and commitments
excluded: scheduling, dispatching, or committing installer resources
answering technical questions that belong to the licence holder

pros.claim: The no-change check-in removes the interpretation a homeowner otherwise supplies, which is that they have been forgotten
pros.example: a week with no movement still produces a short note saying the file is in the permit queue and the next update comes on a stated day

cons.claim: Cadence is a standing time cost on jobs that are already sold and pays nothing additional in a commission model
cons.example: carrying many in-flight jobs consumes selling hours on status work that no commission line compensates

failure_modes: updating only when the homeowner initiates contact
passing on an optimistic date the coordinator floated verbally
contradicting the installer's own customer messaging because the two were never aligned
acceptance_tests: each in-flight job shows a contact log with updates at every stage transition and no gap longer than the stated check-in interval
every date communicated is traceable to an installer record or is explicitly stated as a range with the gating stage named
revisit_triggers: the installer changes its own customer-notification behaviour, creating duplicate or contradictory messaging
in-flight job count rises past what the current cadence can sustain

base.update_signal: cancellation cause coding and homeowner feedback showing whether contact gaps precede the deals that are lost after signature

nodes.definition: Deliver every piece of bad news - a slipped install date, a failed inspection, a redesign after engineering, a crew no-show, a stalled permit - before the homeowner discovers it, and deliver it with structure rather than apology. The protocol is: contact the same day the seller learns it, state plainly what changed, name the gating stage and who owns it without characterizing the partner, give the next verifiable checkpoint instead of a hopeful new date, state what the seller is doing about it, and open or advance a written escalation on the installer's ladder with the job reference. What the protocol forbids is as important: no softening that misleads, no invented cause, no new date the installer has not committed, and no waiting for the weekly update because the news might resolve itself. The seller also records the cause for the cancellation taxonomy and the partner scorecard, because a delay pattern is evidence, not an anecdote.

included: same-day delivery of adverse job news with the gating stage named
written escalation into the installer's ladder
cause capture for scoring and taxonomy
excluded: promising remedies, credits, or compensation the installer has not agreed to
characterizing or disparaging the partner beyond the verifiable facts of status and cause

pros.claim: Hearing it first from the seller preserves the relationship that a discovered delay destroys
pros.example: the homeowner learns of a failed inspection from the seller with the re-inspection step explained, rather than from a neighbour who saw the crew leave

cons.claim: Early honest delivery sometimes converts a homeowner who would have waited quietly into one who now actively reconsiders
cons.example: a candid redesign notice prompts the homeowner to re-open competing quotes during the wait

failure_modes: sitting on news hoping the schedule recovers
replacing a missed date with another uncommitted date, so credibility erodes twice
blaming the installer in terms the seller cannot evidence
acceptance_tests: every adverse event on recent jobs shows a homeowner contact dated on or before the day the seller learned of it
each such event has a written escalation entry with the job reference and the installer contact it went to
revisit_triggers: the same delay cause repeats across jobs, indicating a partner-level issue rather than a job-level one
escalation responses stop arriving inside the agreed expectation

base.update_signal: outcomes of jobs that hit delays, compared between those where news was carried early and those where the homeowner discovered it

nodes.definition: Handle any post-signature change to price, scope, equipment, or payment structure as a re-disclosure event that requires a fresh, informed decision by the homeowner. Adders surface from real site conditions - a main-panel upgrade, roof repair or reroof, structural reinforcement, trenching, a required equipment substitution, a de-rate remedy - and the seller's duty is to explain in writing what changed, why the site requires it, what it does to the total and to any financed payment, and what the homeowner's options are including declining and stopping. The homeowner's fresh agreement is documented in the form the contract and the applicable consumer-protection rules require, and any cancellation right that attaches is restated accurately with its current form verified for the jurisdiction rather than recited from memory. Two behaviours are prohibited outright: absorbing or hiding a change to keep the deal quiet, and presenting an adder as a fait accompli that the homeowner has no say in.

included: written re-disclosure of changed price, scope, and payment consequence
documented fresh consent and the restated option to stop
flagging the cancellation-right obligation class for verification in the jurisdiction
excluded: pricing the adder or deciding its necessity, which is the installer's engineering and commercial call
advising the homeowner on whether to finance the change, which is personalized financial advice

pros.claim: Written re-disclosure with a genuine option to stop is the single strongest defence against a later misrepresentation complaint
pros.example: a panel-upgrade adder is signed with the revised total and payment effect shown, and the homeowner later refers the seller precisely because nothing was hidden

cons.claim: Re-opening the decision at the worst possible moment loses deals that quiet handling would have kept
cons.example: a homeowner who would have absorbed a modest change decides to stop once the revised total is put in front of them

failure_modes: letting the change appear first on a financing document the homeowner reads alone
explaining the change verbally and never documenting the fresh agreement
implying the change is mandatory with no option to cancel
acceptance_tests: every job with an adder shows a dated written re-disclosure and a documented fresh homeowner decision before work proceeded
the re-disclosure states the revised total, the payment consequence, and the option to stop, and any applicable cancellation right is stated with its jurisdiction verified
revisit_triggers: a jurisdiction updates its re-disclosure, cancellation, or home-improvement contract rules
an adder class starts appearing frequently enough that it should be screened for before signature

base.update_signal: a change in the applicable home-improvement contract or re-disclosure rules, or a complaint tracing back to how a change order was presented

nodes.definition: Close the job properly across the stretch that decides whether a customer becomes an advocate: install day, the dark period before permission to operate, activation, and the first billing cycles afterwards. The work is concrete - confirm the punch list is captured and pursued to documented closure, pre-frame and then narrate the wait between panels-on-roof and utility activation including the fact that the homeowner keeps paying their normal utility bill and that any financed payment obligation follows its own schedule, walk the homeowner through monitoring access once the system is live so production is visible to them rather than described by the seller, and sit with the first post-activation statements to read the actual bill against the modelling that was presented, including any true-up or annual reconciliation the tariff uses. The seller explains what the numbers show without re-forecasting or promising, and any gap between modelled and observed production is routed to the installer as a service question rather than explained away.

included: punch-list pursuit to documented closure
narrating the install-to-activation dark period and its billing consequence
monitoring walkthrough and reading the first statements against what was modelled
excluded: diagnosing production shortfalls, inverter faults, or monitoring outages, which is installer or operations-and-maintenance work
re-forecasting savings or making any new production claim, which belongs to the proposal-integrity knowledge base and is never a post-hoc promise

pros.claim: Walking the first bill with the homeowner converts the moment of maximum confusion into the moment of maximum trust
pros.example: the homeowner sees how export credits and the true-up appear on their own statement and stops fearing they were misled

cons.claim: The walkthrough can expose a gap between modelled and observed production that the seller cannot fix and must still stand in front of
cons.example: first-season output tracks below the model because of shading the survey under-weighted, and the seller must route it honestly rather than reassure

failure_modes: declaring the job done at install day while punch items and activation remain open
letting the homeowner meet the pre-activation billing gap without warning
explaining away a production gap instead of opening a service ticket
acceptance_tests: each energized job records punch-list closure evidence, an activation date, a completed monitoring walkthrough, and a first-statement review
any modelled-versus-observed production gap is recorded and routed to the installer with a ticket reference
revisit_triggers: the utility changes tariff, true-up, or export-credit mechanics in a way that changes what the first statements look like
monitoring access or the installer's activation notification process changes

base.update_signal: first-statement reviews across a cohort of energized jobs, showing where homeowners are actually confused and what the walkthrough must cover

nodes.definition: Classify every cancellation at the moment it happens into a cause and an owner, because a transaction-commission business that cannot say why deals die cannot fix anything. The cause classes that recur in residential solar are homeowner remorse inside the cancellation window, financing or credit failure after signature, site or engineering failure discovered at survey, an adder the homeowner declined, roof condition or age requiring work first, homeowners association or landlord refusal, permit or interconnection obstacles, delay-driven loss of patience, competitor re-shopping during the wait, life events such as a home sale or job loss, and complaints of misrepresentation. Each is tagged to an owner - seller, installer, homeowner circumstance, or an authority outside anyone's control - using the job record rather than a guess, and the tag is recorded at the time with a sentence of evidence. The taxonomy feeds the partner scorecard, the qualification practice upstream, and the seller's own honesty about which losses were self-inflicted.

included: the cause classes and owner attribution
capture at the moment of cancellation with an evidence sentence
feeding the scorecard and the upstream qualification practice
excluded: pipeline conversion and sales-cycle modelling, and the economic modelling of cancellation into deal value, which belong to the market-models and lead-economics knowledge base
any stated cancellation rate as a figure rather than as a measured property of the seller's own book

pros.claim: Cause coding turns an unhappy month into an addressable list, and separates losses the seller caused from losses nobody could prevent
pros.example: a quarter's cancellations cluster on declined adders, pointing at a pre-signature site screen rather than at the installer

cons.claim: Homeowners often give a polite reason rather than the real one, so the coding carries a systematic bias toward blameless causes
cons.example: a cancellation recorded as 'moving' was actually driven by a neighbour's warning about the installer

failure_modes: recording cancellations with no cause at all
coding every loss as homeowner circumstance to protect the partner or the seller's own record
coding late from memory once the details have blurred
acceptance_tests: every cancelled deal in the ledger carries a cause class, an owner tag, a date, and one sentence of evidence from the job record
the coding is reviewed for the blameless-cause bias by checking a sample against the contact log
revisit_triggers: a cause class appears that the taxonomy does not cover
cause distribution shifts materially between periods or between partners

base.update_signal: a period of coded cancellations large enough to show whether causes cluster by partner, by stage, or by the seller's own practice

nodes.definition: Treat a homeowner's stated intent to cancel as an instruction to be executed, not an objection to be handled. The required actions are immediate and documented: acknowledge in writing the same day, tell the homeowner the contract's stated cancellation route and how to use it, pass it into that route without delay, and confirm back when it is processed. Within that, exactly one legitimate question is available - asking, once and without pressure, whether something specific went wrong that the seller could fix, offered as information rather than as a hurdle - and if the homeowner declines to discuss it or repeats the decision, the conversation ends. What is prohibited is the whole retention playbook this vertical is criticized for: delaying or losing the request, requiring a call before processing, re-pitching after a clear decision, implying penalties or consequences that the contract does not create, or suggesting cancellation is unavailable. Cancellation windows, the required form of notice, and any cooling-off obligation are an obligation class whose current form must be verified for the jurisdiction and the sale setting rather than recited from training.

included: same-day written acknowledgement and routing through the contract's cancellation channel
the single non-pressuring cause question and where it stops
flagging cancellation-window and notice rules as an obligation class to verify per jurisdiction
excluded: any advice to the homeowner about the legal consequences of cancelling, which requires their own counsel
retention techniques, incentives, or delay of any kind

pros.claim: Cancelling someone cleanly protects the reputation asset better than saving them badly, and sometimes returns them later
pros.example: a homeowner who cancelled without friction refers a relative the following year and says the seller made it easy

cons.claim: Immediate clean processing forfeits deals that a legitimate conversation might genuinely have rescued, and triggers the chargeback exposure at once
cons.example: a homeowner cancelling over a fixable delay is processed before an escalation could have resolved the underlying stall

failure_modes: treating the cancellation as an objection and running a rebuttal
letting the request sit unprocessed while a manager attempts a save
reciting a remembered cancellation window instead of the contract's terms and the current jurisdictional rule
acceptance_tests: every cancellation request shows a written acknowledgement dated the same day and a routing record into the contract's stated channel
no cancellation record shows more than one cause enquiry, and none shows contact after the homeowner repeated the decision
the cancellation-window and notice-form rules relied on are documented with the source and the date they were verified for the jurisdiction
revisit_triggers: a jurisdiction changes cancellation-window, notice, or door-to-door sale rules
a partner changes the contractual cancellation route or its processing behaviour

base.update_signal: a regulatory or contractual change to cancellation rights, or a complaint alleging that a cancellation request was obstructed or delayed

nodes.definition: Administer the money side of a cancelled or reversed deal as a contract mechanism: reconcile, evidence, dispute where warranted, and learn. When a statement shows a deduction or offset, the seller matches it to a named trigger clause in the agreement and to a deal-level record with dates, requests the backup detail if the statement does not show which job and which trigger, and checks the arithmetic of the offset order and any lookback. Where the deduction does not match a trigger or the underlying event is contradicted by the job record - the deal actually installed, the cancellation fell outside the lookback, the funding failure was reversed - the seller disputes in writing inside the contractual window with the job evidence attached and tracks it to resolution. The same records feed the partner read: isolated corrections are ordinary, while recurring unexplained deductions, statements without deal-level detail, or disputes that go unanswered are a partner-quality signal rather than an accounting nuisance.

included: reconciliation of each deduction to a trigger clause and a deal record
the written dispute inside the contractual window with evidence attached
treating deduction patterns as partner-quality evidence
excluded: deciding whether to pursue legal remedies, which requires the seller's own counsel
commission-structure design and personal income planning across the pay cycle, which belong to the market-models and lead-economics knowledge base

pros.claim: Deal-level reconciliation converts an opaque statement into a checkable ledger and recovers deductions that were simply wrong
pros.example: a deduction on a job that did install is reversed once the activation date and the milestone record are attached to a written dispute

cons.claim: Disputing costs relationship capital with the partner whose scheduling attention the seller depends on
cons.example: a seller who disputes several statements in a row finds coordinator responsiveness cooling on live jobs

failure_modes: accepting statements without deal-level backup because chasing them is tedious
missing the contractual dispute window
treating recurring unexplained deductions as normal instead of as a partner signal
acceptance_tests: every deduction on a statement is reconciled to a named trigger clause and a deal record, with unresolved items listed
each dispute is filed in writing inside the contractual window with the job evidence attached and tracked to a written outcome
revisit_triggers: a deduction type appears that the clause map does not explain
dispute outcomes start arriving late, unanswered, or inconsistent with the agreement

base.update_signal: a run of reconciled statements showing which deduction types recur, how often disputes succeed, and how quickly the partner responds

nodes.definition: Gate every referral and review request behind objective conditions that make advocacy honest, so the business never harvests goodwill it has not yet earned. The conditions are checkable from the ledger rather than from a feeling: the system is installed and activated by the utility, production is visible in monitoring and consistent with what the system should be doing, the punch list is documented as closed, the first post-activation statement has been walked through, no service ticket or complaint is open, and the homeowner has not asked to be left alone. A job that fails any condition is not ineligible forever - it is a job with work still to do, and the gate's real function is to redirect the seller's energy from asking to finishing. Introductions that a homeowner volunteers before the gate are accepted graciously, but no campaign, sequence, or incentive is run against an unfinished job.

included: the objective eligibility conditions and their evidence in the ledger
the redirect from asking to finishing when a condition fails
the treatment of volunteered introductions before the gate
excluded: designing referral compensation classes and their economics, which belong to the market-models and lead-economics knowledge base
qualifying the referred homeowner, which is front-of-funnel work in the sibling knowledge base

pros.claim: Asking only after verified completion means advocacy is grounded in an experience the customer can actually describe
pros.example: a referred neighbour hears specifics about activation and the first bill because the referring homeowner has already lived them

cons.claim: The gate delays referral asks past the emotional peak at install day, when enthusiasm is highest
cons.example: a delighted homeowner on install day is not asked, and by activation the excitement has cooled into ordinary satisfaction

failure_modes: asking at install day because the customer seems happy
treating the gate as permanent disqualification instead of a work list
recording eligibility from impression rather than from ledger evidence
acceptance_tests: each job in the ledger carries an eligibility flag derived from the stated conditions with the evidence date for each
a sample of referral and review requests shows every one was sent after its job cleared the gate
revisit_triggers: a condition proves to be a poor proxy for genuine satisfaction and needs replacing
referral yield from gated cohorts diverges sharply from what the gate predicted

base.update_signal: referral and review outcomes by cohort, showing whether jobs that cleared the gate actually produce advocacy and whether any condition is doing no work

nodes.definition: Make the referral request in a way that a homeowner would describe accurately to the person they are introducing. The request is specific rather than generic - naming the kind of situation the seller can help with, so the homeowner is not asked to canvass their address book - and it is made once per occasion with an explicit, easy way to decline that is honoured permanently. Any compensation attached to a referral is disclosed to both the referring homeowner and the referred party before any appointment, in the form the applicable obligation class requires for the jurisdiction and the compensation type, which must be verified rather than assumed. The seller never uses the referred relationship as leverage on either side, never implies the referring homeowner has vouched for outcomes they cannot know, and treats the introduction as a warm start that still runs the ordinary honest qualification. A referral that arrives is also acknowledged back to the referrer with the outcome the referred party consents to share, which is what keeps the flow alive.

included: the specific, single, opt-out-respecting ask
disclosure of any referral compensation to both sides as an obligation class to verify
acknowledgement back to the referrer within what the referred party permits
excluded: the economics and legality classes of referral compensation structures themselves, which belong to the market-models and lead-economics knowledge base
qualifying or selling to the referred homeowner, which is front-of-funnel work

pros.claim: A specific ask with a clean decline route produces better-matched introductions and costs nothing in goodwill
pros.example: asking whether anyone nearby has mentioned high bills yields a neighbour with the same roof orientation rather than a random name

cons.claim: Disclosing compensation can make a warm introduction feel commercial and suppress referrals that would otherwise have come
cons.example: a homeowner who was happy to introduce a friend hesitates once a disclosed reward is on the table

failure_modes: repeated asks that turn a satisfied customer into an avoided call
leaving a referral reward undisclosed to the referred party
letting the warm introduction shortcut honest qualification of the new homeowner
acceptance_tests: the request script in use states the specific situation sought and an explicit decline route, and opt-outs are recorded and honoured
any referral compensation is documented as disclosed to both parties before the first appointment, with the applicable obligation class and its verification date recorded
revisit_triggers: a jurisdiction or platform changes the disclosure rules attaching to referral compensation
opt-out or non-response rates rise, indicating the ask has become intrusive

base.update_signal: referral conversion and opt-out data by cohort, plus any change in the disclosure obligation class for referral compensation in the jurisdiction

nodes.definition: Build the public half of the reputation asset within rules the seller verifies rather than assumes. Review requests go only to customers past the verified-happy gate, are made neutrally without steering the content or the rating, and are never gated - the practice of soliciting only those expected to be positive is treated here as prohibited, alongside incentivised reviews without the disclosure the platform and the jurisdiction require, reviews written by anyone other than the customer, and any remedy conditioned on removing or editing a review. Responses to public criticism follow their own discipline: reply promptly and civilly, never disclose the customer's private details or contract terms in public, state what the seller is doing rather than arguing the facts in the thread, move the substance to a private channel, and fix the underlying cause so the same review is not written again by the next customer. Public claims about production, savings, or timelines carry the same mechanism-based honesty as the sales conversation, since a marketing page is a representation like any other.

included: neutral, ungated review requests to gate-cleared customers
the response discipline for public criticism
the honesty standard for public performance claims
excluded: advertising strategy, brand building, and paid channel work, which belong to the lead-economics knowledge base
asserting what a specific platform's or jurisdiction's review rules currently are, which must be verified against the platform's own policy and the applicable authority

pros.claim: A public record that includes an imperfect review answered well is more persuasive than an unbroken wall of praise
pros.example: a prospective homeowner reads a delay complaint and the seller's factual response about the permit stage and takes the appointment anyway

cons.claim: Public reputation is disproportionately shaped by failures the seller neither caused nor controls, and cannot be corrected in public without exposing private details
cons.example: a review blames the seller for a utility activation queue, and the accurate explanation risks disclosing account specifics

failure_modes: soliciting reviews only from customers expected to be positive
offering an incentive for a review without the required disclosure
arguing with a reviewer in public or conditioning a fix on the review coming down
acceptance_tests: review requests are documented as sent to all gate-cleared customers in a period without selection by expected sentiment
each public response is checked to contain no private customer detail and no condition attached to a remedy
the platform and jurisdiction rules relied on for solicitation and incentives are recorded with their verification date
revisit_triggers: a platform updates its solicitation, incentive, or response policies
a pattern in review content points at a fixable operational cause

base.update_signal: a platform policy change, a regulator action on review practices, or a shift in the themes appearing in the seller's own public reviews

nodes.definition: Work a complaint that has escalated - to a public review, a consumer-protection body, a licensing authority, a funder, or a lender's dispute process - as a reputation event with a fixed sequence rather than as an argument to win. Acknowledge quickly and in a channel the complainant chose, reconstruct the job from the record including the dated expectation log, the contact log, the disclosures, and the change orders, and separate what is a defect, what is a communication failure, what is a misunderstanding, and what is outside anyone's control. Route each element to whoever owns it - workmanship and warranty to the installer, financing mechanics to the lender or funder, representation and communication to the seller - and be honest in attribution including when the answer is that the seller got it wrong. Remedies are never conditioned on withdrawing the complaint, private customer details never appear in a public response, and where an allegation touches misrepresentation the seller treats it as an identity-level failure to be investigated against the record rather than deflected. Where a regulator or licensing body is involved, the seller responds factually, within the stated time, and takes advice from their own counsel on anything beyond the facts.

included: acknowledgement, record reconstruction, element-by-element routing, honest attribution
the prohibition on conditioning remedies and on public disclosure of private details
factual, timely response to a regulator or licensing body with the seller's own counsel engaged where needed
excluded: legal representation, settlement strategy, or interpretation of a regulator's authority, which requires counsel
diagnosing or remediating the physical defect, which is the installer's work

pros.claim: A reconstructed record turns a he-said-she-said complaint into a resolvable factual matter, often in the seller's favour
pros.example: the dated expectation log and re-disclosure signature answer an allegation about a hidden panel-upgrade cost in a single reply

cons.claim: Honest attribution sometimes means telling the complainant and the record that the seller's own practice failed, with lasting consequences
cons.example: the log shows the seller stated a single install date rather than the cohort range, and the complaint is substantively correct

failure_modes: responding from memory and being contradicted by the record
offering a remedy conditioned on the complaint being withdrawn
letting the installer answer for the seller's own representations or vice versa
acceptance_tests: each escalated complaint has a dated acknowledgement, a reconstructed record pack, an element-by-element routing list, and a written outcome
no remedy in the record is conditioned on withdrawal of a complaint, and no public response contains private customer detail
revisit_triggers: a complaint alleges misrepresentation, which triggers a review of the sales and disclosure practice itself
complaints cluster on one partner, one crew, or one stage of the process

base.update_signal: the pattern and disposition of escalated complaints over time, and any regulator or platform guidance that changes what a response must contain
